en.title: Sort by Number of 1 Bits
en.description:
Sort first by the number of 1s in the binary representation in ascending order, then by integer value in ascending order for equal counts; all duplicate elements are kept.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and solution; bounds missing from the source and corrections to the examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers. Full original bounds: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤a[i]≤1000000.
en.output: Output the n sorted integers, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 2 3 7 15 31; 1 2 4 3 5; 1 3 3. They were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Use (number of binary 1s, integer value) as the sort key.
